manifest.name: OneFeed — One way to read your feeds
manifest.description: Turn feeds from different websites into one calm, consistent reading experience that you control.

page.boardDescription: Continue reading, open a supported website, or pause OneFeed from the launch center.
page.onboardingDescription: OneFeed is installed. Learn about supported websites, core features, and how to get started.
page.optionsDescription: Configure local display filters for OneFeed.

zhihu.name: Zhihu
zhihu.scope: Home, Hot List, questions, and articles

v2ex.name: V2EX
v2ex.scope: Home categories, recent topics, VXNA, and topic pages

hackerNews.name: Hacker News
hackerNews.scope: News, Newest, Ask, Show, and Jobs

thirtySixKr.name: 36Kr
thirtySixKr.scope: News channels, article lists, and article pages

board.introDescription: Choose a website and return to focused reading.
board.enabledNote: Pause OneFeed to restore the original page on every website.
board.pausedNote: OneFeed is paused. Websites will open with their original pages.

onboarding.heroIntro: OneFeed rearranges different websites into one calm, consistent reading interface that you control. The content stays on its original platform; the reading experience becomes yours.
onboarding.tryHackerNews: Try it now on Hacker News
onboarding.experienceNote: No sign-in required · Opens in a new tab and starts automatically
onboarding.previewLabel: Illustration of OneFeed arranging several websites into one reading interface
onboarding.previewBodyOne: Consistent typography, a clear hierarchy, and only the actions you need.
onboarding.previewBodyTwo: Keep the content and the choice to return to the original page at any time.
onboarding.toggleShowOriginal: Click to show the original page
onboarding.startTitle: There is nothing new to learn.
onboarding.stepOneDescription: Visit any supported feed listed below. You do not need to launch OneFeed separately.
onboarding.stepTwoDescription: OneFeed organizes the content automatically while preserving reading, scrolling, and essential interactions.
onboarding.stepThreeDescription: Use the switch on the right side of the page or the launch-center switch to pause OneFeed immediately.
onboarding.pinDescription: Open Chrome's extensions menu, find OneFeed, and pin it. You can then open the launch center from its icon.
onboarding.supportedTitle: Start with a website you know.
onboarding.supportedNote: Select any website to visit it. OneFeed only takes over pages that have been adapted.
onboarding.featureLayoutDescription: Titles, text, images, and interactions from different platforms share one clear structure.
onboarding.featureThemeDescription: A restrained reading theme reduces page noise and supports light and dark appearances.
onboarding.featureReadingDescription: Keep infinite scrolling and pagination without sacrificing browsing efficiency for a calmer interface.
onboarding.featureActionsDescription: Actions such as votes and comments are delegated to the original website; when that is not reliable, OneFeed takes you back to the source.
onboarding.controlTitle: The original page is one click away.
onboarding.controlDescription: The floating page switch and launch-center switch share the same state. Pausing OneFeed restores the original page immediately.
onboarding.trustTitle: Your reading stays in your browser.
onboarding.trustDescription: OneFeed reads a supported page only while you have it open, and only to create the unified reading interface.
onboarding.closingTitle: Make the next feed a little more focused.

toggle.disableLabel: Disable OneFeed and show the original page
toggle.showOriginal: Click to show the original page

filter.validationCondition: Add at least one filter condition.
filter.validationValue: Complete every keyword or author condition.
filter.author: Author
filter.localOnly: Rules run locally on this device.
filter.backLabel: Return to the OneFeed launch center
filter.introDescription: Rules only change what OneFeed displays. They never modify, delete, or upload content from the original website.
filter.indexDescription: Every condition in a rule must match; content is hidden when any rule matches.
filter.pausedSummary: Rules are preserved but are not filtering content.
filter.quickTitle: Handle the most common noise first
filter.hideSeenDescription: Use locally stored read markers to avoid showing the same items again.
filter.hideRecommendedDescription: Applies only when the platform provides a recommendation reason; missing data never causes a match.
filter.emptyDescription: Start with a keyword, author, or content type to create your first filter rule.

reader.continue: You've read this far · Keep scrolling to load more
reader.answersFinished: You've finished the answers on this page
reader.repliesFinished: You've finished the replies on this page

block.videoUnsupported: Your browser cannot play this video.
